children: , the enterprise-software and customer-data giant, pushed deeper into the AI stack at Dreamforce by creating a bridge between its business data and outside AI models, Investor's Business Daily reported. Shares fell approximately 1.4% to $252.10 Wednesday, based on the latest quoted price. The strategy is increasingly clear: Salesforce does not want AI sitting beside its softwareit wants AI running through the workflows customers already use.

AIforce connects Salesforce data, applications and autonomous agents with platforms including Slack and Anthropic's Claude, while the company also introduced Koa, a model built with Nvidia's Nemotron technology and Salesforce's massive store of CRM data. The business model matters just as much as the technology. Salesforce is leaning harder into consumption-based pricing, meaning revenue growth increasingly depends on how much customers actually use these AI tools rather than how many software seats they purchase. That gives Salesforce a potentially larger monetization runway, but it also raises the bar: customers need to keep finding enough value to increase usage.

Agentforce annual recurring revenue has already topped $1.5 billion, equivalent to roughly 3.2% of the midpoint of Salesforce's $46.25 billion fiscal-year revenue guidance. Add Data 360 and that comparison climbs to about 8.4%, showing that Salesforce's AI-and-data push has moved beyond experimentation. The valuation picture adds another angle: the stock at $252.10 sits 26.52% below the $343.08 GF Value estimate shown in the chart. That gap looks substantial, but closing it will depend on Salesforce proving that easier AI distribution can translate into durable consumption growth without sacrificing its projected 20.1% GAAP operating margin.

title: Salesforce Falls 1.4% as AIforce Faces a $46 Billion Conversion Test
